subject: VIP account: cascading throttles during morning peak
messages:
From: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@solix.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Solix Support <support@solix.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: morning surge — VIP customers seeing 504s / error spike

Hi Vivek / Laura,

We're hitting a sharp increase in 504s and token-generation timeouts across our VIP traffic this morning (since ~07:50 PDT). Error rate has climbed to ~28% for short-chat flows; median latency is up ~3x and p99s are off the charts. This looks like something in your serving stack — customer support is fielding calls.

Attached are a small sample of request traces and a bucket of headers/latency stats (svc-logs-20290525.txt). Diego and our SREs are on the line. We need an ETA on mitigation — this is impacting the top 5% of our ARR.

Can you triage and advise next steps? We'll need either a quick rollback or a configuration change we can validate.

Thanks,
Amelia Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability, Solix AI
Amelia.Ruiz@solix.ai

Attachments: svc-logs-20290525.txt (6.2 KB)

Subject: Re: Urgent: morning surge — VIP customers seeing 504s / error spike

Amelia — thanks for the ping and the logs.

Quick note: I'm standing up a focused runbook with Jonas and Laura. First-pass asks: can you confirm the traffic pattern (burst vs constant) and whether the affected requests are short-chat or long-context streaming? That will help us decide whether this is batch-triggered or caching/KV pressure.

Jonas — can you take the lead on an initial triage (kernel/caching telemetry) and propose an immediate mitigation (canary to smaller batch size or pin to non-prefetch lane)? Laura — I'll loop you on customer comms and any credit/SLA asks.

I'll escalate to ops leadership if this doesn't stabilize within the hour.

— Vivek
VP, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Amelia Ruiz <amelia@solix.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: morning surge — initial ops findings

Hi all — initial findings from the morning window (07:45–08:20 PDT):
- Observed repeated HOL blocking on priority lane when the KV prefix cache is rebalanced; priority lane worker threads get queued behind large batch prefetches.
- KV cache miss rate spiked concurrently with a surge of mid-sized batch requests (batch_size distribution shifted +40%). This leads to increased cache churn and KV eviction thrash.
- Result: per-token service time increases and backpressure propagates to front-end routing -> 504s on short-chat flows.

Attached: svc-logs-20290525.txt with trace markers and early flamegraph.

Immediate mitigations proposed (ordered):
1) Reduce max_batch_size for VIP route to 8 and enforce per-tenant batching window of 25ms (fast rollback, low risk).
2) Temporarily disable cross-tenant prefetch for the affected hosts to reduce KV churn.
3) Trigger a KV cache warmup for Solix prefixes (best-effort) and raise eviction thresholds.
4) If the above doesn't help within 20–30m, fallback to the stable model variant (lower memory footprint) for VIPs; ops will coordinate traffic split.

I'll apply (1) as a canary now and monitor. Note: applying (2) requires a short restart of the prefetch worker on the pool (estimated 2–3m).

Jonas
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: svc-logs-20290525.txt (sample), playbook ref: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1123

From: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@solix.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Diego Varela <diego@solix.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: morning surge — initial ops findings

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the quick analysis. We're seeing the same timing and the reduction to batch_size=8 would help test if this is the culprit.

Quick context for impact: about 18 of our enterprise sessions dropped mid-conversation and our NPS team is already reporting escalations. If this is a runtime config regression on your side, we'll need a commercial remedy (credit) and a timeline for a permanent fix. Our Exec of Product is watching.

Please confirm when the canary is applied and any customer-visible degradations during restarts.

— Amelia

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: morning surge — account & SLA coordination

Team — looping in finance and customer ops. Per Amelia: VIP revenue at risk; they want an ETA and the possibility of credit.

Proposal: authorize an immediate customer goodwill credit up to $10k while we validate root cause. I'll own the commercial outreach. Operational asks:
- Jonas: proceed with (1) and (2) now; please attach metrics for the change window.
- Vivek / Ben / Marissa: if we need to fallback to the stable model variant, confirm expected cost delta and whether we can automate rollback if perf regresses.

Attaching kernel-profiles.pdf from runtime to show memory/kernel pressure observed in the window.

Laura Bennett
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kernel-profiles.pdf (4.1 MB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ruiz <amelia@solix.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 May 2029 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: actions taken and next steps (canary applied)

Amelia / team — quick status update and plan.

What we did (12:05–12:20 PDT):
- Applied canary: reduced max_batch_size to 8 for Solix VIP route and enforced a 25ms batching window.
- Disabled cross-tenant prefetch on the affected host pool; restarted prefetch worker (2.5m blackout) as per runbook.
- Warmed Solix prefixes via targeted prefetch; bumped eviction threshold for those partitions.

Observed impact: within 10m of the canary we saw error rate drop from ~28% to ~4% for VIP flows and median latency returned to baseline. p99 is trending down but we'll watch for secondary effects.

Next steps (owner):
- Jonas: monitor SUP-1123 for 2h and report metrics every 15m (jonas_weber).
- Laura: coordinate the $10k goodwill credit and confirm with Amelia (laura_bennett).
- Ops follow-up: create a config hardening change to prevent excessive batch-size shifts and add a prefetch throttle guard by EOD (jonas_weber / marissa_cole).

We will keep the canary in place for 4 hours and consider a controlled rollback to the standard config only after a successful stability window. If any regression appears, we'll immediately trigger fallback to the stable model variant (lower memory).

Amelia — apologies for the disruption and thank you for the rapid signal and logs — that helped with a fast mitigation. Please let us know if you want the credit handled sooner; Laura will confirm.
